info.title: Character builder HTTP API
info.description: JSON over HTTP. Everything the screens do, a tool can do with an access key (`Authorization: Bearer <key>`, made in the settings). See API.md for the conventions and an example from an empty character to the PDF.

tags.name: Sheet copies
tags.description: Copies of the sheet a player keeps and changes freely, and the play state. Kept apart from the character; the builder never reads them. Same access as the character: owner, game master of the owner's campaign, an access key of either; anyone else gets 404.

tags.name: Campaigns
tags.description: Whoever makes a campaign leads it (game master) and invites players with one link per campaign (`/join/{token}`), which they send themselves; the builder mails no invitations; the game master sees their names, never their addresses. The game master reaches the players' characters that belong to the campaign; a character in no campaign stays private. A player sees only their own characters and the campaigns they are in. Anyone else gets 404.

tags.name: Live help
tags.description: Several people build one character together, live over a WebSocket: its owner, the game master of its campaign, and anyone the owner gives the character's help link (`/help/{token}`, 12 hours, one per character). See API.md, section Live help.

tags.name: MCP
tags.description: The public MCP server and the download for running one yourself. Outside `/api`; see API.md, section MCP.

get.description: Answers as long as the process serves requests, also when no content package is loaded. Lists the loaded packages; `warnings` names rejected package folders, an empty package list or a failed start. Not part of the router; used by Docker.
This file, openapi.json (OpenAPI 3.1), as it is in the repository. Without a login. Read by the API reference at `/api/docs`.

This description as a page in the browser: every route to read, and to try with an access key. Without a login. Everything on it, scripts and fonts included, comes from this server; a request made with "Try it" goes straight to this server, and the key is not stored in the browser.

post.description: Makes an account with a name and, if given, a mail address (only a way back in; nothing is mailed now). The server makes the first password (five words and a number) and returns it in this answer only, and sets the session cookie: the player is logged in at once. At most 10 new accounts per hour per IP.

name.description: What the player wants to be called. Trimmed; 1 to 80 characters, one line. Not unique.

email.description: Optional. A way back in if every password is lost. Several accounts may give the same address.

language.description: Language of the screens and of the password's words (`de`, `en`); default `de`.

201.description: The account and its first password, shown this once.

post.description: Any account: a name or a mail address, and a password. The password finds the account (case, spaces instead of dashes and spaces around it do not matter); the name or the address must be that account's (case and spaces around it do not matter). If none fits and `login` is an address: an account from before, made when passwords were mailed, with that password, once. Its old password is then swapped for a new one, returned in this answer only (`password`); from then on only the new one works. Every failure gets the same answer. Sets the session cookie. Tools use an access key instead. Failed logins are limited per IP (30 in 15 minutes), and per address for accounts from before (10 in 15 minutes).

login.description: The account's name or its mail address. Trimmed.

200.description: Logged in. With `password` for an account from before, at its first login: the new password, shown this once.

post.description: For whoever lost every password and gave a mail address: mails one link per account with this address, in one mail, each named with the account's name. A link works once, for 30 minutes, and shows a new password (`POST /api/auth/reset/use`). The mail holds no password. The answer is the same whether the address has an account or not; nothing is mailed if it has none. At most 3 mails per hour per address and 10 per IP. The mail is in the language of the first account with the address.

language.description: Language of the mail if an account has none (`de`, `en`).

202.description: Sent if the address has an account; the same answer if not.

post.description: The token from the link `/login/reset/<token>` of the mail. Works once, within 30 minutes: makes a new password (`origin: "reset"`, no name), returned in this answer only, and sets the session cookie. The account's other passwords stay. If the account already has 10, its oldest goes. At most 20 tries per 15 minutes per IP.

200.description: Logged in; the new password, shown this once.

post.description: Ends the session of the cookie and clears it. With an access key there is nothing to end.

delete.description: Deletes the account with its sessions, access keys, every character, the campaigns it leads (the players keep their characters) and its places in other campaigns. Cannot be undone.

patch.summary: Change name, mail address, language, units or the print choice
patch.description: `name` is what the player is called (shown to game masters); `email` the way back in, `null` removes it. `units` maps a dimension to a unit; `null` follows the language's default again. `print` keeps what the download dialog offers next time; fields left out stay as they are.

mailReminder.description: "Later": no more reminder to add an address, on any device. It does not come back.

200.description: The account with the new settings.

422.description: `unknownUnit`, `designNotAvailable` (a planned design that is not drawn yet)

get.description: Oldest first. The passwords themselves are not stored and never shown again; `name` is what the owner called one.

post.description: Another password for the account, for example one per device or one on paper; each one logs in. Only with the session cookie (the settings screen); a request with a key gets `403 keyCannotMakePasswords`. `password.secret` is in this answer only. At most 10 per account.

name.description: What the password is for, in the owner's words. One line. Without one, the password has no name (`null`) and the screen names it by the day it was made.

201.description: The new password, shown this once.

delete.description: Takes effect at once: a login with it fails. Sessions opened with it stay. The account's last password cannot be deleted (`422 lastPassword`): without one, nobody gets back in.

get.description: Oldest first. The keys themselves are not stored and never shown again; `name` is what the owner called a key, `hint` its first characters.

post.description: Only with the session cookie (the settings screen); a request with a key gets `403 keyCannotMakeKeys`. `key.secret` is in this answer only.

name.description: What the key is for, in the owner's words, for example "the laptop at home". Trimmed; 1 to 80 characters after trimming, one line. Shown in the list only.

201.description: The new key, shown this once.

delete.description: Takes effect at once: the next request with the key gets `401 keyNotValid`.

get.description: Name and description in one language: `lang` if the package has it, else the account's language, else the package's first.
The parts of the package as the package format specification (SPEC.md) describes them.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Package id, or a package with extensions: `base+ext1+ext2` (extensions sorted).

get.description: Text keys follow SPEC.md section 10.2, for example `<thing>.name`, `<thing>.short`, `<thing>.explain.what`, `choice.<id>.question`. A missing text is `null`, never filled from another language.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Package id, or a package with extensions: `base+ext1+ext2` (extensions sorted).

fallbacks.description: Texts of an extension this language does not have, taken from the extension's fallback language: key → that language. Show them marked as such.

get.description: Newest change first. Your own characters only; a game master finds the players' characters in `GET /api/campaigns/{id}`.

post.description: An empty draft at version 1. Without `level`, the package's default level. With `campaignId`, the character belongs to that campaign; it must be one you play in or lead.

extensions.description: Extensions of the package to switch on; none if left out.

campaignId.description: A campaign you play in or lead; left out or null for none.

404.description: `packageNotFound`, `campaignNotFound` (also a campaign you neither play in nor lead), `extensionNotFound` (not an extension of this package)

parameters.name: help
parameters.description: The draft's help link token, for someone who is neither its owner nor the game master of its campaign (see Live help). Without a working one, someone else's draft answers 404.

404.description: `draftNotFound` (also someone else's character: it looks exactly like a missing one)

get.description: Your own character, a player's in a campaign you lead, or one whose help link you hold (`?help=`; `draft.access`). Every draft route below works on the first two; opening and changing (this, explain, level, answers, pools, level-up, finish) also on the third.

patch.summary: Change the level or the extensions
patch.description: Answers stay; what the level no longer asks is kept in `inactiveAnswers`. During a raise, a level at or below `levelBefore` ends the raise. `extensions` switches the package's extensions for this character (package format SPEC 17): the answer is evaluated with them. One goes off only while no answer comes from it, else `409 extensionInUse` with the choices to change first.

parameters.name: help
parameters.description: The draft's help link token, for someone who is neither its owner nor the game master of its campaign (see Live help). Without a working one, someone else's draft answers 404.

version.description: The draft version the change was made on (optimistic locking).

extensions.description: All extensions to have on afterwards.

404.description: `draftNotFound` (also someone else's character: it looks exactly like a missing one), `extensionNotFound`

choices.description: The choices whose answers come from the extension.

404.description: `draftNotFound` (also someone else's character: it looks exactly like a missing one)

delete.description: Only the owner deletes; a game master gets `403 ownerOnly`.

get.description: The parts a value of the character adds up from, each with its source, as the screen explains it ("15 + 2 = 17"). Data, not sentences: sources name ids, their words are in the package texts (`value.<id>.name`, the thing's name, the choice's title), as in `GET /api/drafts/{id}`. Parts from the same source are added up; parts of 0 are left out. `parts` is null when they would not add up to the number (a minimum or maximum cut it).

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: Value id from the package (`evaluation.values` lists them).

parameters.name: help
parameters.description: The draft's help link token, for someone who is neither its owner nor the game master of its campaign (see Live help). Without a working one, someone else's draft answers 404.

404.description: `draftNotFound` (also someone else's character: it looks exactly like a missing one), `valueNotFound` (the package has no such value)

put.description: The answer's shape depends on the choice's `kind` (see `Answer`). `answer: null` removes the answer. An answer that does not fit now is refused with `changeRejected`; a partial `pickMany` answer is stored and the choice stays open.

parameters.name: help
parameters.description: The draft's help link token, for someone who is neither its owner nor the game master of its campaign (see Live help). Without a working one, someone else's draft answers 404.

version.description: The draft version the change was made on (optimistic locking).

404.description: `draftNotFound` (also someone else's character: it looks exactly like a missing one)

put.summary: Answer a step with one shared list
put.description: For steps with `pool`: all picks of the step at once; the server spreads them over the step's choices.

parameters.name: help
parameters.description: The draft's help link token, for someone who is neither its owner nor the game master of its campaign (see Live help). Without a working one, someone else's draft answers 404.

version.description: The draft version the change was made on (optimistic locking).

404.description: `draftNotFound` (also someone else's character: it looks exactly like a missing one)

put.description: Only for packages with tracks (`evaluation.tracks`, package format SPEC 9.7): the track (a thing of the tracks choice) of each level from 2 on, in level order. Levels left out go to the first track, the answer of the tracks choice. Answers of a track taken away stay and count again once it is back. A track whose condition to be added does not hold is still taken; it shows in `evaluation.tracks.unfit` and keeps the character from being complete.

parameters.name: help
parameters.description: The draft's help link token, for someone who is neither its owner nor the game master of its campaign (see Live help). Without a working one, someone else's draft answers 404.

version.description: The draft version the change was made on (optimistic locking).

tracks.description: The track of each level from 2 on.

404.description: `draftNotFound` (also someone else's character: it looks exactly like a missing one)

post.description: Every answer stays; only what the new levels add is asked (`levelUp`). With nothing to answer the character is finished again at once. With tracks (`evaluation.tracks`), `tracks` names the track of each new level in order; a level left out goes to the track of the level before. A track the character does not have yet is added only if `evaluation.tracks.options` allows it (else 422 `changeRejected` with `trackNotAllowed`).

parameters.name: help
parameters.description: The draft's help link token, for someone who is neither its owner nor the game master of its campaign (see Live help). Without a working one, someone else's draft answers 404.

version.description: The draft version the change was made on (optimistic locking).

tracks.description: Only with tracks: the track of each new level, in level order.

404.description: `draftNotFound` (also someone else's character: it looks exactly like a missing one)

put.summary: Put a character into a campaign
put.description: Only the owner, and only into a campaign they play in or lead; `null` takes it out of every campaign. The character itself does not change: its `version` stays.

campaignId.description: A campaign you play in or lead, or null for none.

404.description: `draftNotFound`, `campaignNotFound` (also a campaign you neither play in nor lead)

parameters.name: help
parameters.description: The draft's help link token, for someone who is neither its owner nor the game master of its campaign (see Live help). Without a working one, someone else's draft answers 404.

version.description: The draft version the change was made on (optimistic locking).

404.description: `draftNotFound` (also someone else's character: it looks exactly like a missing one)

get.description: Everything the sheet says, as one JSON model: texts in one language, quantities in the account's units, sections in the package's order with conditions decided, the places a player writes on (`field`, `usesField`, `playedByField`), for each value the values that change with it, and the full texts of the character's rows and cards. Language and units from the account settings, like the PDF; a game master sees a player's character in their own. Made on every request, never stored. `origin` says the character's level, when it last changed in the builder (`changedAt`) and the package version (`packageVersion`); a kept copy keeps the same of the original it was made from (`fromLevel`, `fromChangedAt`, `fromPackageVersion`), so the screen can say "the original changed since" without comparing models.

200.description: The sheet model: the original, made now.

404.description: `draftNotFound` (also someone else's character: it looks exactly like a missing one)

get.summary: Designs a sheet can be printed in
get.description: The designs the server draws, with a name and one line about each in every screen language, for a choice before printing. `default` is the one used when none is asked for. Cards and rules texts look the same in every design.

A4 PDF/A with the parts asked for, always in the order sheet, cards, rules texts; one page count through the file. Without `parts`: the sheet, then the cards, exactly as before parts existed. Language and units from the account settings. Made on every request, never stored. A game master prints a player's character in the game master's language and units.

parameters.name: parts
parameters.description: Comma-separated, one or more of `sheet` (the character sheet), `cards` (one card per thing marked as a card, with cut lines), `texts` (the full rules texts of every feature and card, two columns, under the name of what brought them). Default: `sheet,cards`.

parameters.name: design
parameters.description: How the sheet looks; ids from `GET /api/sheet-designs`. Default: the first design there (`verbose`). A design that is planned but not drawn yet answers `400 designNotAvailable`.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: Which sheet: `original` (made from the character as it is now, in the account's language and units) or the id of a kept copy (printed as kept, in the copy's language and units; its cards and rules texts are the original's). Anything else answers `404 versionNotFound`.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: `empty`: a sheet to write on. `filled`: the play state written into the fields; ticks beyond what a field holds are cut, fields the sheet does not have are skipped.

parameters.name: tz
parameters.description: The reader's time zone (`Europe/Zurich`). A copy that kept the name it was made with is printed as the screen names it, by the minute it was made in this zone; the file name of a copy names it too. Without it, the server's zone.

Content-Disposition.description: `attachment` with the character's name; with `parts`, the parts' names after it ("Mira - Sheet, Cards.pdf").

400.description: `badQuery` (a parameter with a value the API does not know; `parameter` and `value` name it), `designNotAvailable` (a planned design not drawn yet; `designs` lists those that are)

404.description: `draftNotFound` (also someone else's character: it looks exactly like a missing one), `versionNotFound` (neither `original` nor a kept copy of this character)

409.description: `notFinished`, `packageUnavailable` (the original, also for a copy's cards and rules texts), `copyUnreadable` (a kept copy stored in a shape this server no longer prints)

get.summary: The kept copies of a character's sheet
get.description: Oldest first, without models, and the original as it is now (`original`) to tell which copies it moved away from. Also while the character is not finished, and while its package is not loaded.

200.description: The copies and the original's stamp.

opened.description: The copy this account opened last; null for the original.

max.description: How many copies a character may have.

404.description: `draftNotFound` (also someone else's character: it looks exactly like a missing one)

post.summary: Keep a copy of the sheet
post.description: Copies the original as it is now, in the language and units of whoever asks, named "Meine Fassung vom <date>" in that language unless `name` is given. With `model`, the copy is that model instead: the original as the viewer loaded it with the first change already in, so the first change makes a copy in one request. Its `origin` must be the original as it is now (`level`, `changedAt`, `packageVersion`), else `409 originalChanged`. At most 50 copies per character; the new copy becomes the asker's opened version.

404.description: `draftNotFound` (also someone else's character: it looks exactly like a missing one)

get.summary: A kept copy with its model
get.description: Exactly as it was kept or last changed: a level, other answers, a package update or another account language leave it as it is.

put.summary: Rename a copy or change its model
put.description: `name`, `model` or both, with the version it was read at. The model is checked for shape only (`SheetModel`); like on paper, anything may be written in and nothing follows from it. Its `origin` is ignored: a copy's origin always comes from the copy.

version.description: The copy version the change was made on.

post.summary: Where the PDF breaks the sheet's pages
post.description: For the screen to break its pages where the paper does: the page (from 0) and grid column each section of the given model starts on in the PDF of the sheet alone in this design, with the character's play state written in. A section the PDF splits counts on the page of its first part; `null` for one the design does not show.

422.description: `languageNotSupported`: the model's language has no page words

put.summary: Which version of the sheet opens next time
put.description: Per account: a copy of this character, or `null` for the original. The online sheet opens it next time; making a copy sets it too.

get.description: What is written and rubbed out at the table, for the original and every copy alike. A field the shown sheet does not have is skipped by the screen; ticks over what a field holds are cut there. The state itself is never trimmed.

200.description: The play state; `version: 0` and `{}` while nothing is stored.

404.description: `draftNotFound` (also someone else's character: it looks exactly like a missing one)

put.summary: Write the play state, or rub out every tick
put.description: The whole state at once (`state`), or `clearChecks: true` to remove every count of ticks and keep the rest (a rest; the builder does not know what a rest is). With the version it was read at; the first write names 0.

404.description: `draftNotFound` (also someone else's character: it looks exactly like a missing one)

get.summary: Campaigns you lead or play in

post.description: You lead it. At most 50 per account.

name.description: One line; trimmed; no control characters.

get.description: The game master gets the invitation link, their own characters in this campaign, and the players with theirs; a player gets the campaign only, without the link.

name.description: One line; trimmed; no control characters.

delete.description: Game master only. The campaign and its player list go; every character stays with its owner, in no campaign.

post.description: Game master only. Replaces the campaign's invitation link: the old one stops working at once, whoever joined with it stays a player. At most 30 per hour per game master.

parameters.name: playerId
parameters.description: The player's id, or `me` to leave the campaign yourself.

delete.description: The game master removes any player; a player removes only themselves (`me`). The characters stay with the player and leave the campaign; the game master no longer reaches them.

post.summary: Start a character for a player
post.description: Game master only. Like `POST /api/drafts`, but the character is the player's (`owner`) and belongs to this campaign; you build it with the draft routes.

extensions.description: Extensions of the package to switch on; none if left out.

campaignId.description: Optional; if given, this campaign's id.

parameters.name: playerId
parameters.description: The player's id from the campaign (a UUID).

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: The last part of the invitation link (`/join/{token}`).

get.description: The campaign an invitation link opens and who leads it, by name. Shown before joining; also without an account. Logged in, `you` says whether one leads the campaign (`gameMaster`) or plays in it already (`player`); a member gets this for a replaced link too, which opens nothing for anyone else. At most 60 lookups (this and joining) per 15 minutes per IP, found or not.

you.description: Logged in: `gameMaster` or `player` if one is in the campaign already; null otherwise, and without an account.

post.summary: Join a campaign by its invitation link

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: The last part of the invitation link (`/join/{token}`).

post.description: Joins the campaign as a player. Joining again, or as its game master, changes nothing and answers the same. The game master can then see, change and print the characters you put into the campaign; nothing else of yours. At most 50 players per campaign; counts against the same 60 lookups per 15 minutes per IP as `GET /api/invites/{token}`.

get.summary: The MCP address, opened in a browser
get.description: A browser (`Accept` with `text/html`) is sent to the page about the MCP server, `/mcp/setup`. Anything else gets `405`: the server takes POST only.

405.description: Not a browser: the MCP server takes POST only.

post.description:
An MCP server over Streamable HTTP without sessions: every request carries its access key as `Authorization: Bearer cbk_...` and is answered on its own, as plain JSON, never as an event stream. No session cookie, no key in the address. The tools are those of the zip (`packages/mcp`) and reach this API in process with that key, so they can do exactly what the key can do over the API.

Refusals come in order: `429` (more than 120 requests a minute from one address, with or without a key), `413` (body over 1 MB), `403` (an `Origin` other than the server's public address; programs send none), `401` (no key, or one that is unknown, withdrawn or past its end; `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`).

requestBody.description: A JSON-RPC 2.0 message of the MCP protocol (`initialize`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`, ...). `Accept` must name `application/json` and `text/event-stream`.

202.description: A notification was taken; no answer.

401.description: No access key, or not a valid one. The message says where to make one.

WWW-Authenticate.description: `Bearer realm="character-builder"`, with `error="invalid_token"` for a key that is not valid.

413.description: The body is larger than 1 MB.

429.description: Too many requests from this address.

502.description: The tools could not reach the API.

get.description: The MCP server to run yourself, the same for everyone, without a login (`curl -O`, `wget`, a browser): `server.mjs` (one file, Node 20 or newer; private over stdio with a key, public over HTTP without one), `config.json` (`{ "baseUrl": <this server's BASE_URL>, "key": "" }`), `claude_desktop_config.json` (an entry with the placeholders `PATH` and `KEY`), `README.md` (English) and `ANLEITUNG.md` (German). No key, nothing personal. Made once when the server starts; `ETag` answers `If-None-Match` with `304`.

ETag.description: Changes with a new build or a new address.

304.description: The zip named in `If-None-Match` is still the one.

503.description: `baseUrlNotSet` (the server has no public address configured), `mcpPackageMissing` (this build has no `server.mjs`).

get.summary: The help link of a character
get.description: Owner only. The link while it works, to show it again; `null` for none, or one that ended.

403.description: `ownerOnly` (the game master of the campaign; they need no link), `crossSite`

post.description: Owner only. Makes the character's help link; the one before stops working, and whoever helps with it is out at once, also live. Ends after 12 hours. At most 30 per hour per account.

403.description: `ownerOnly` (the game master of the campaign; they need no link), `crossSite`

delete.description: Owner only. The link stops working; whoever helps with it is out at once, also live. Without a link, changes nothing.

403.description: `ownerOnly` (the game master of the campaign; they need no link), `crossSite`

get.description: Whose character a help link opens, shown before helping; also without a login. Counts against the same 60 lookups per 15 minutes per IP as an invitation, found or not.

yours.description: True when you own the character: you need no link for it.

live.description: The path of the live channel with this link: `/api/live/drafts/{id}?help={token}`.

get.summary: The live channel of a character (WebSocket)
get.description: A WebSocket (`Upgrade: websocket`), not a JSON route, and the one live channel of a character: everyone on it sees who else is there and hears of every stored change at once, whoever made it and however (over this channel, the HTTP API with the cookie or a key, or the MCP server: `source.via` is `browser`, `api` or `mcp`), and may answer. Login as everywhere: the session cookie or `Authorization: Bearer <key>`; the handshake must come from this site (`Origin`). Who is neither the owner nor the game master of the character's campaign adds `?help=<token>`. A browser window adds its own id, `?clientId=`, the same it sends as `X-Builder-Client-Id` on its HTTP changes; the MCP server sends `X-Builder-Client: mcp`. A refused login or a character you may not reach closes the connection after one `error` message with code 4401 or 4404 (as 401 and 404 here). The messages are in API.md, section Live help.

parameters.name: clientId
parameters.description: The browser window's own id (1–64 characters `A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -`), as it sends it in `X-Builder-Client-Id`; shown in `presence` and on its changes. Anything else is ignored.

101.description: Switching to the WebSocket protocol. Then JSON messages both ways (API.md, Live help).

403.description: The handshake came from another site. No body.

default.description: Not a WebSocket handshake, or the server is not ready. No body.

accessKey.description: An access key from the settings. A request with an `Authorization` header is judged by the key alone.

sessionCookie.name: __Host-session
sessionCookie.description: The browser's session cookie after login (`session` on plain-HTTP trial setups).

Unauthorized.description: `notLoggedIn` without cookie or key; `keyNotValid` with a key that is unknown, withdrawn or past its end.

CrossSite.description: A change sent from another site.

ServerError.description: A bug in the builder (`internal`) or in the package (`packageRuleError`).

ErrorCode.description:
Every error code the API answers with. Stable and English; screens word them in the player's language.

- `badJson`: 400. The body is not JSON.
- `badRequest`: 400. The body has the wrong shape; `issues` lists `{ path, message }`.
- `badQuery`: 400. A query parameter has a value the API does not know; `parameter` and `value` name it.
- `designNotAvailable`: 400 (PDF) or 422 (settings). A planned sheet design that is not drawn yet; `designs` lists those that are.
- `notLoggedIn`: 401. No session cookie and no `Authorization` header.
- `keyNotValid`: 401. The `Authorization` header holds no valid access key (unknown, withdrawn, past its end, or not `Bearer <key>`).
- `wrongLogin`: 401. No account fits this name or address and this password.
- `crossSite`: 403. A change sent from another site (`Origin` or `Sec-Fetch-Site`).
- `keyCannotMakeKeys`: 403. Access keys are made on the settings screen only, never with a key.
- `keyCannotMakePasswords`: 403. Passwords are made on the settings screen only, never with a key.
- `notFound`: 404. No such API path.
- `draftNotFound`: 404. No draft with this id in this account.
- `keyNotFound`: 404. No access key with this id in this account.
- `passwordNotFound`: 404. No password with this id in this account.
- `inviteNotFound`: 404. No campaign has this invitation link (unknown, or replaced by a new one).
- `helpLinkNotFound`: 404. No character has this help link (unknown, replaced, withdrawn or older than 12 hours).
- `resetLinkInvalid`: 404. The link back in is unknown, used already or older than 30 minutes.
- `packageNotFound`: 404. No loaded package with this id.
- `languageNotFound`: 404. The package has no texts in this language.
- `valueNotFound`: 404. The draft's package has no value with this id.
- `versionNotFound`: 404. No such version of the sheet to print: neither `original` nor a kept copy of this character.
- `methodNotAllowed`: 405. The path exists, the method does not.
- `versionConflict`: 409. The draft moved on; `current` holds its state now.
- `notFinished`: 409. The character is not finished (PDF) or not finished and not in a raise (level-up); `open` lists the open choices.
- `packageUnavailable`: 409. The draft's package is not loaded right now; `packageId` names it.
- `copyUnreadable`: 409. A kept copy stored in a shape this server no longer prints; `version` names it.
- `bodyTooLarge`: 413. The body is larger than 64 KiB.
- `jsonRequired`: 415. The body is not `application/json`.
- `changeRejected`: 422. The rule core refused the change; `reason` says why (see `ChangeError`).
- `incomplete`: 422. Finishing with open choices; `open` lists them.
- `languageNotSupported`: 422. The account's language cannot be printed with this package; `languages` lists those that can.
- `tooManyKeys`: 422. The account has the most access keys allowed (`max`).
- `tooManyPasswords`: 422. The account has the most passwords allowed (`max`).
- `lastPassword`: 422. The account's last password cannot be deleted.
- `unknownUnit`: 422. No loaded package offers this unit for this dimension.
- `tooManyAttempts`: 429. Too many failed logins, new accounts, new invitation links, invitation or help link lookups, new help links or links back in; `retryAfter` seconds, also in `Retry-After`.
- `tooManyRequests`: 429. Too many PDFs; see `Retry-After`.
- `internal`: 500. A bug in the builder.
- `packageRuleError`: 500. The package's rules could not be worked out (a bug in the package); `message` says where.
- `mailFailed`: 502. The mail server refused the mail with a link back in; nothing was changed.
- `mailNotConfigured`: 503. The server has no mail (or no `BASE_URL` for links) set up; no link back in can be mailed.
- `baseUrlNotSet`: 503. The server has no public address configured (`BASE_URL`), so the MCP zip cannot say where the builder is.
- `mcpPackageMissing`: 503. This build of the server has no `server.mjs` for the MCP zip.

JsonRpcError.description: A refusal of the MCP server, the way the MCP library answers one: JSON-RPC 2.0 without an id. `message` says in English what to do.

name.description: What the player wants to be called.

email.description: The way back in, if one was given; null for none.

language.description: Language of screens, mails and the PDF.

units.description: Chosen unit per dimension; a missing dimension follows the language.

mailReminder.description: Whether to remind the owner to add a mail address: none given, and not answered with "Later" (`mailReminder: false` in the settings).

name.description: What the owner called the password; display only. `null` when it has no name: the screen names it by `origin`, or by the day it was made.

origin.description: Made by the server: `first`, the account's first password (also the one after logging in an account from before); `reset`, one from a link back in. `null`: made by the owner.
Made by the server: `first`, the account's first password (also the one after logging in an account from before); `reset`, one from a link back in. `null`: made by the owner.

secret.description: The password: five words and a number, joined by dashes. Shown only in this answer; the server keeps only its hash.

name.description: What the owner called the key. Keys made before names existed carry the day they were made (`2026-10-04`).

hint.description: The first characters of the key, to tell keys apart.

secret.description: The key. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <secret>`. Shown only in this answer.

extensions.description: The extensions this package is put together with (empty for a base alone): id, version, languages, publishable, names, and the keys of their things and choices.

Package.description: A loaded package without its texts. The shape of each part is the package format (SPEC.md sections 5 to 13). `GET /api/packages/demo+demo-tides` is the package `demo` with its extension `demo-tides`, as a draft with that extension uses it.

packageVersion.description: Package version the draft was last changed with.

extensions.description: Extensions of the package switched on for this character (package format SPEC 17); empty for none.

version.description: Grows with every change; send it with the next change.

levelBefore.description: The level a raise started from, until the character is finished again.

campaignId.description: The campaign the character belongs to (one its owner plays in); null for none.

answers.description: Stored answers by choice id; see `Answer`.

owner.description: Whose character it is, by name. It stays theirs, whoever changes it.

access.description: `owner`: your own. `gameMaster`: a player's, in a campaign you lead; you may open, change, raise and print it, not delete it. `helper`: someone's who gave you its help link; you may open and change it while the link works, nothing else.

tracks.description: With tracks (package format SPEC 9.7): the track of each level from 2 on, in level order; empty when every level is in the first track (or the package has no tracks).

ValueExplanation.description: Where a value comes from: its number and the parts it adds up from.

parts.description: In order of appearance; their amounts add up to `total`. Null if the value cannot be told apart as a sum.

amount.description: Negative for a part that takes away.

source.description:
- `start`: the fixed number the value starts at (or the number in its formula).
- `choice`: set or raised by the answer to this choice (`choice` is its id; for a copy, the copy's id; a choice a thing brought along is in `evaluation.steps[].grantedBy`).
- `thing`: given by a thing the character has (`thing` is its id); with more than one track, a thing in a track also names it (`track`) and the level reached in it (`trackLevel`).
- `values`: worked out from these other values (`level` included).
- `unclear`: two ways gave the same number; no source rather than a wrong one.

packageAvailable.description: False if the draft's package is not loaded now; `evaluation` and `summary` are null then.

levelUp.description: While a raise lasts (and in the answer of the raise): what it brought.

DraftView.description: What every draft route answers: the stored draft and everything the rule core derives from it.

anyOf.description: For a `{ tracks: true }` argument: the tracks with their levels, most first, on a tie the one taken first.

line.description: Arguments of the package text `summary.line`: a thing key, a number, or the tracks with their levels, per variable.

newSteps.description: Steps with `atLevel > from`, in step order.

newChoices.description: Choices with `atLevel > from`, in step order.

openSteps.description: Every step not `done`, in step order.

steps.description: The steps asked now, in order.

choices.description: Every choice asked now, by id.

things.description: Everything the character has, in the order it was gained.

values.description: Every value of the package, worked out.

inputs.description: Values set directly by an answer, with the choice that set them.

raises.description: Points added to values by `raise` answers, per value in step order.

marks.description: Format 0.10: things picked again in a choice with `options.owned`, with those choices.

open.description: Choices that still need an answer (missing, incomplete or invalid, not optional), in step order. Empty when `complete`.

complete.description: True when nothing is open and no track is `unfit`.

inactiveAnswers.description: Stored answers of choices not asked now (kept for going back).

Evaluation.description: Everything the rule core derives from the package and the answers. A tool reads `open` for what to answer next, `choices[id]` for how, and the package texts for the words.

choices.description: Choice ids of the step, in order.

atLevel.description: Character level from which the step is asked.

track.description: The track the step's choices came through (package format SPEC 9.7), if all came through one.

trackLevel.description: With `track`: the level in that track at which the step is asked.

options.description: What this choice offers, also what another choice of the list holds now (the choice's own options leave those out).

PoolState.description: One shared list for all choices of a step; answer it with `PUT /api/drafts/{id}/pools/{step}`.

everyone.description: Every character of the package has it (`flow.grants`); such a thing has no `step`.

step.description: Step that brought it to the character; absent for things every character has.

count.description: How many of it, if more than one: the counts of every grant that gives it, added up.

track.description: The track it belongs to: a track itself, or a thing that came through one (package format SPEC 9.7).

id.description: The choice id; a copy is `<choice>@<where picked>`.

copyOf.description: Copies only: the declared choice whose rules and texts it uses.

status.description: `missing`: no answer; `incomplete`: fits, more needed; `invalid`: the stored answer does not fit now (`problem`); `answered`; `info`: nothing to answer.

options.description: pickOne, pickMany: the thing keys that may be picked now.

upTo.description: pickMany: fewer than `count` is complete too.

recommended.description: pick choices: recommended picks, best first. distribute: a full recommended answer `{ method, assign }`.

badges.description: pick choices: badge text key by option.

held.description: Things the character has that an offered option is about.

givenBy.description: Problem `duplicate` because a grant gives a pick anyway (often in a later step): each such pick with the thing that grants it.

track.description: The track the choice came through (package format SPEC 9.7); a choice of an added track is a copy `<choice>@<track>`.

ChoiceState.description: One choice as it stands. Words come from the package texts in one language: the question is `choice.<id>.title`, `.question`, `.intro` (for a copy, of `copyOf`; with `textVariant`, `choice.<id>.variant.<v>.*`), each option `o` has `<o>.name`, `<o>.short`, `<o>.explain.what`, `<o>.explain.table` and maybe `<o>.goodIf`.

counts.description: How many of a thing in `things`, where the grant gives more than one.

Problem.description: Why an answer does not fit.

ChangeError.description: Why the rule core refused a change.

anyOf.description: distribute: `method` is an index into the choice's `methods`; `assign` gives a number per value. For the method `raise`, the points added on top.

Answer.description: An answer; its shape follows the choice's `kind`.

role.description: Yours in this campaign: you lead it, or you play in it.

joinedAt.description: When you joined it as a player; null if you lead it.

inviteUrl.description: The campaign's invitation link, `<BASE_URL>/join/<token>`. Only for its game master, and only on a single campaign (`GET`/`POST /api/campaigns`), not in the list.

id.description: The player's id; used in the player routes.

name.description: The player's name. Mail addresses of other people are never given out.

Player.description: A player as the game master sees them.

characters.description: For the game master: their own characters in this campaign, newest first. For a player: null.

id.description: The player's id; used in the player routes.

name.description: The player's name. Mail addresses of other people are never given out.

characters.description: Every character of the player, newest first.

players.description: For the game master: the players with their characters. For a player: null (players do not see each other).

CampaignView.description: A campaign; what it shows depends on your role in it.

SheetCopy.description: A kept copy of the sheet, without its model.

fromLevel.description: Level of the original it was made from.

fromChangedAt.description: When the character had last changed when the copy was made (the original's `origin.changedAt` then).

fromPackageVersion.description: Package version of the original it was made from.

language.description: Language the copy is written in; it does not follow the account.

units.description: Units the copy is written in.

SheetCopyView.description: A copy with its model. The model's `origin` is `{ kind: "copy", name, createdAt, fromLevel, fromPackageVersion, fromChangedAt }`.

OriginalStamp.description: The original as it is now, without building it. Differs from a copy's `fromLevel`, `fromChangedAt` or `fromPackageVersion`: the original changed since the copy was made.

packageVersion.description: Null while the character's package is not loaded.

finished.description: False while the character has open choices; then there is no original sheet, the copies stay readable.

PlayValue.description: A number, a text, or a count of ticks.

PlayState.description: The play state: field id of the sheet (`field`, `usesField`, `playedByField`) to its value. At most 1000 fields.

PrintChoice.description: What the download dialog offers first: the last download's choice. Until one was made: only the sheet, in the first design, empty.

HelpLink.description: A draft's help link, as its owner sees it.

url.description: The link to hand over: `/help/{token}` on the server's public address.

token.description: 22 characters; opens the draft with `?help=` and on the live channel.

languages.description: The extension's own languages; the first is its fallback language. A text missing in another language comes from it.

dependsOn.description: The package it extends, as in its manifest.

publishable.description: False: content that may not be shared. A sheet with content from it says so.

ExtensionEntry.description: An extension a character of the package may switch on (package format SPEC 17). `name` and `short` in the package entry's `language`.

allowed.description: May take the next level: a track the character has, or one whose condition to be added holds now.

notMet.description: Only if not allowed: the things whose `addRequires` does not hold, the track itself first, then (with `addRequiresCurrent`) tracks the character has. The package's sentence for each is the text `<thing>.addReason`.

TracksState.description: Only for packages with tracks (package format SPEC 9.7): things of one choice that collect levels.

choice.description: The tracks choice; the builder's step for the levels comes right after its step.

first.description: The first track (the answer of the tracks choice), null while there is none that counts.

levels.description: The track of each character level, level 1 first; empty without a first track.

list.description: Each track with its levels, in the order taken.

from.description: The character level of its first level.

options.description: Every option of the tracks choice for the next level (a raise).

unfit.description: Added tracks whose condition to be added no longer holds (checked as the character was before the level that added them). They still count; the character is not complete until this is empty.
